sample_unit: responses (36 Google results and 36 ChatGPT-3.5 answers)

links.outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT-3.5 and Google answers versus NIH sixth-grade recommendation
links.effect: Mean grade level 16.1 ± 3.6 for ChatGPT-3.5 and 11.0 ± 2.9 for Google; none of 72 responses met the NIH sixth-grade criteria.
links.quote: Of 72 total responses across both search modalities, none met NIH readability criteria at the sixth-grade level.

links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-3.5 answers to patient questions about bone cancers
links.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 answers were at a fourth-year undergraduate reading level (16.1 ± 3.6); Google answers were more readable (11.0 ± 2.9).
links.quote: This corresponds to the eleventh grade reading level for Google and a fourth-year undergraduate student level for ChatGPT-3.5.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the readability of ChatGPT-3.5 answers compared to Google search results for patient queries about musculoskeletal malignancies. It does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
